description: A public repo: the files are written, the confidentiality notice is given, and .gitignore is not edited
prompt: /spike-loop:poc-start Webhook HMAC check. Tier 1. Repo visibility: public. Deal: none. Question: can a small receiver verify an HMAC-SHA256 webhook signature computed over the raw request body? Assumptions: 1. the signature is over the raw body, which could be wrong if the provider signs the parsed JSON; 2. the header holds a hex digest, which could be base64 instead. Success check: manual, send the provider's test event and see 'signature ok' in the receiver log. In scope: the HMAC check. Out of scope: persistence and retries. Timebox: 2 hours.

headings: ## Manual check (only if verify.sh cannot do it)

graders.pattern: Docs\ folder:\ `poc\-spec/`\.\ All\ paths\ are\ relative\ to\ the\ repo\ root\.\ At\ session\ start\ read\ `poc\-spec/POC\.md`\ and\ the\ last\ 40\ lines\ of\ `poc\-spec/LOG\.md`\.\ Stay\ within\ `poc\-spec/POC\.md`\.\ Park\ new\ ideas\ in\ `poc\-spec/LOG\.md`\ under\ Later\.\ Never\ claim\ done\ without\ the\ output\ of\ `\./verify\.sh`\ or\ the\ manual\ check\.\ Hand\-offs,\ specs\ and\ plans\ for\ this\ PoC\ go\ under\ `poc\-spec/`\.
